- **Output:** `/home/mara/cwe-bench/sibling2/out/screener/31448.json`
- **Trust decision:** filenames passed in by the caller, and header values decoded while parsing, are assumed to contain no CR/LF when they go into composed MIME headers. The decision is made in `src/Message/Helper/MultipartHelper.php:314` (building an attachment) and in the decoders `src/Header/Part/MimeToken.php:46` and `src/Header/Part/ParameterPart.php:65-71` (parsing). The old CR/LF strip in `MimeToken` runs before decoding, so encoded CR/LF got through.
- **pattern_fit:** A+B. The fix covers the attachment helper plus two parser decoders in another package. At the pinned commit five routes into the same sink are still unfixed; the strongest are the raw `$mimeType`/`$encoding` in the same function and the public `UUEncodedPart::setFilename`, whose output is written by the external stream-decorators package.
- **Strongest lever:** the "how-type" parse-then-re-emit boundary. Decoded `name*=`/encoded-word values get written back out (`src/Message/Helper/PrivacyHelper.php:84-87`, `src/Stream/MessagePartStream.php:161`), and a solver can argue "the parser should return the true decoded value". Over-broad fixes that strip CR/LF break header folding.
- **Biggest red flag:** this is a small library, so it may be `tiny_repo` (I didn't measure the size). I also couldn't confirm what the external `UUStream` does with the filename. No formal red flags are set.
